objects.description: Generic indexing helper that maps enum values to stable indices, optionally sorted by a comparator. Provides begin/end over sorted enum values and at() to map a value to its index. A transparent specialization supports heterogeneous lookup when E is void.

Comparator functor that orders enum values by their magic_enum names. The void specialization is transparent and supports comparing enum values to strings or characters depending on provided Cmp. Aliases provide common presets including case-insensitive ordering.

objects.definition: struct raw_access_t {};
objects.description: Tag type used to select raw-access overloads (bit patterns and raw string/number constructors or conversions) for containers like bitset.

Generic bidirectional iterator adaptor that iterates over a range while filtering elements using a predicate and projecting values via a getter. Used to expose iterators of containers like set over enum domains.
A fixed-size associative array whose indices are enum values of E, optionally remapped by a custom indexing. Wraps std::array<V, enum_count<E)>. Provides checked and unchecked element access by enum.

A small, fixed-size bitset keyed by enum E values. Provides set/test/reset/flip, bitwise ops, iteration via conversions, string and raw representations, and an implicit conversion back to E when E is a flags enum.

A sparse set of enum E values backed by an internal bitset over the enum domain. Provides set-like API (insert/erase/find/bounds/contains) with O(1) operations using the enum indexing order defined by comparator Cmp.

objects.definition:

using default_indexing = detail::indexing<E>;
objects.description: Alias template selecting the default indexing strategy for enum E (identity for natural enum order, or computed order otherwise).

Tag type used as the default Result parameter for enum_switch to signal that the result type should be deduced from the callable. Empty struct; no state.

objects.definition: struct nonesuch {};
objects.description: Sentinel type indicating absence of a valid type or non-invocable cases in internal meta-functions.

objects.definition:
template <>
struct std::common_type<magic_enum::detail::nonesuch, magic_enum::detail::nonesuch> : magic_enum::detail::identity<magic_enum::detail::nonesuch> {};
objects.description: Specialization of std::common_type so that common_type of nonesuch and nonesuch resolves to nonesuch.

enum_subtype is referenced as a dependent type for selecting the reflected subset of an enum (e.g., all values vs. flags). It is not defined in this header; it comes from magic_enum.hpp. No definition present here.

Traits-like holder used for ADL customization of enum range, flags-ness, and prefix length. Returned by customize::adl_info() and by magic_enum_define_range_adl specializations to encode settings via type. Not directly constructed at runtime.

Primary customization point for per-enum settings. Users may specialize enum_range<E> or provide an ADL-detected base to set min, max and optionally is_flags and prefix_length via adl_info_holder. Default min/max are from macros.
Internal tag enum indicating which customization kind is selected for names/type names: default, invalid (suppress), or custom string.
Lightweight pair-like class used as a return type for customize::enum_name and customize::enum_type_name. Encodes either a custom string, default handling, or invalid/suppressed via customize_tag.

objects.definition:
template <typename T>
struct supported
#if defined(MAGIC_ENUM_SUPPORTED) && MAGIC_ENUM_SUPPORTED || defined(MAGIC_ENUM_NO_CHECK_SUPPORT)
  : std::true_type {};
#else
  : std::false_type {};
#endif
objects.description: Compile-time trait that reflects whether the current compiler is supported by magic_enum. Specializes to std::true_type or std::false_type depending on macros.
Trait detecting presence and validity of customize::enum_range<T>::is_flags boolean member.
Computes the minimum reflected value for enum T, defaulting to MAGIC_ENUM_RANGE_MIN or using customize::enum_range<T>::min if provided.
Computes the maximum reflected value for enum T, defaulting to MAGIC_ENUM_RANGE_MAX or using customize::enum_range<T>::max if provided.
Internal lightweight string view used in compile-time parsing when standard string_view cannot be used directly in certain contexts.
Compile-time fixed-size string holder producing a NUL-terminated buffer and a string_view view. Used to store type and enumerator names at compile time.
Character comparator adaptor that performs case-insensitive comparison using a nested Op (default std::equal_to). Used for name matching.
Helper aggregate for compile-time scanning of valid enum values across a range: holds a count and a bitmap of which offsets are valid.
Internal SFINAE helper yielding type R only when the boolean template parameter is true and compiler support is available.
Trait yielding whether T is a scoped enum (enum class), i.e., not implicitly convertible to its underlying type.
Trait yielding whether T is an unscoped enum (implicitly convertible to its underlying type).
Conditional alias to std::underlying_type for enum types; intentionally left incomplete for non-enums.
Internal classification of how to interpret an enum when reflecting: as common consecutive values or as bit flags (powers of two).

functions.name: magic_enum::containers::to_array
functions.signature:
template <typename E, typename T, std::size_t N>
constexpr std::enable_if_t<(enum_count<E>() == N), array<E, std::remove_cv_t<T>>> to_array(T (&a)[N]);
functions.description: Builds a magic_enum::containers::array indexed by enum E from a C-style array with exactly enum_count<E>() elements. The values are copied from the input array into the enum-indexed container. Use when you have a compile-time sized C array and want an enum-indexed array.
requirements: E must be an enum supported by magic_enum (enum_count<E>() must be a valid nonzero constant expression).
N must equal enum_count<E>() (enforced at compile time via enable_if).
T can be any element type; it is decayed to remove cv-qualifiers.
Input parameter must be a reference to a C array of size N; pointer arguments are not accepted.
Function is constexpr; arguments must be usable in constant evaluation if you rely on compile-time evaluation.

functions.name: magic_enum::containers::make_array
functions.signature:
template <typename E, typename... Ts>
constexpr std::enable_if_t<(enum_count<E>() == sizeof...(Ts)), array<E, std::remove_cv_t<std::common_type_t<Ts...>>>> make_array(Ts&&... ts);
functions.description: Constructs a magic_enum::containers::array indexed by enum E from a parameter pack of values. The number of provided values must equal enum_count<E>(). Elements are converted to a common decayed type and forwarded into the result in enum order.
requirements: E must be an enum supported by magic_enum (enum_count<E>() must be a valid nonzero constant expression).
The number of arguments must equal enum_count<E>() (enforced by enable_if).
Ts... must have a valid common_type; elements are converted to std::remove_cv_t<std::common_type_t<Ts...>>.
Callers should ensure the provided values correspond to the intended enum order of E (i.e., in the same order as enum_values<E>()).
Function is constexpr; arguments must be usable in constant evaluation if you rely on compile-time evaluation.

functions.name: magic_enum::containers::get
functions.signature:
template <auto I, typename E, typename V, typename Index>
constexpr std::enable_if_t<(std::is_integral_v<decltype(I)> && I < enum_count<E>()), V&> get(array<E, V, Index>& a) noexcept;
functions.description: Returns a reference to the Ith element stored in an enum-indexed array. This is the integral index overload, constrained to valid indices at compile time.
requirements: I must be an integral non-type template parameter such that 0 <= I < enum_count<E>() (enforced at compile time).
E must be an enum supported by magic_enum; array<E, V, Index> must be a valid instantiation.
Noexcept; function must not throw.

functions.name: magic_enum::enum_flags_name
functions.signature:
template <typename E>
[[nodiscard]] auto enum_flags_name(E value, char_type sep = static_cast<char_type>('|')) -> detail::enable_if_t<E, string>
functions.description: Returns a string containing the names of all flags set in value for an enum type E treated as flags. Names are joined using sep (default '|'). If value contains bits not corresponding exactly to a non-zero combination of known flag enumerators, or any participating enumerator has no name, an empty string is returned. Intended for converting a valid flags value to a delimited name string.
requirements: E must be an enum type supported by magic_enum and reflected as enum_subtype::flags; otherwise a static_assert will fail at compile time.
value must be a non-zero bitwise OR of known single-flag enumerators of E; otherwise the function returns an empty string.
If any enumerator involved in value has an empty name, the function returns an empty string.
sep is the character used to join multiple names; default is '|'.

functions.name: magic_enum::enum_flags_cast
functions.signature:
template <typename E>
[[nodiscard]] constexpr auto enum_flags_cast(underlying_type_t<E> value) noexcept -> detail::enable_if_t<E, optional<std::decay_t<E>>>
functions.description: Parses an underlying integer into a flags enum value of type E. Returns an engaged optional if value is a valid non-zero combination of known flag enumerators, otherwise returns an empty optional.
requirements: E must be an enum type supported by magic_enum and reflected as enum_subtype::flags; otherwise a static_assert will fail at compile time.
For sparse enums: every bit set in value must correspond to a known single-flag enumerator; value must be non-zero. Otherwise returns empty optional.
For non-sparse enums: value must be within [min, OR-of-all-enum-values]; otherwise returns empty optional.
If the enum has no reflected values (count == 0), returns empty optional.

functions.name: magic_enum::enum_flags_contains
functions.signature:
template <typename E>
[[nodiscard]] constexpr auto enum_flags_contains(E value) noexcept -> detail::enable_if_t<E, bool>
functions.description: Checks whether value is a valid non-zero combination of known flag enumerators of enum type E. Returns true if enum_flags_cast<E>(static_cast<underlying_type_t<E>>(value)) succeeds.
requirements: E must be an enum type supported by magic_enum and reflected as enum_subtype::flags; otherwise a static_assert will fail at compile time.

functions.name: magic_enum::enum_flags_test
functions.signature:
template <typename E>
constexpr auto enum_flags_test(E flags, E flag) noexcept -> detail::enable_if_t<E, bool>
functions.description: Tests whether all bits set in flag are present in the flags set flags. Returns false if flag is zero; otherwise returns (flags & flag) == flag.
requirements: E must be an enum type supported by magic_enum; intended for use with flags-style enums.
flag equal to 0 is considered not a flag and yields false.

functions.name: magic_enum::enum_flags_test_any
functions.signature:
template <typename E>
constexpr auto enum_flags_test_any(E lhs, E rhs) noexcept -> detail::enable_if_t<E, bool>
functions.description: Tests whether lhs and rhs share any common flag bit. Returns true if (lhs & rhs) != 0; otherwise false. If either operand is zero, the result is false.
requirements: E must be an enum type supported by magic_enum; intended for use with flags-style enums.

functions.name: magic_enum::detail::format_as
functions.signature:
template <typename E, std::enable_if_t<std::is_enum_v<std::decay_t<E>>, int> = 0>
std::string magic_enum::detail::format_as(E e)
functions.description: Converts an enum value to a human-readable string using magic_enum. If the enum type is recognized and is a flags enum, returns the combined flag names; if it is a scoped/unscoped enum, returns the enumerator name. If no name is available (unsupported value/type), returns the integer value as a decimal string. Intended for use by formatter integrations, but can be used directly to get a string for any enum.
requirements: E must be an enum type (std::is_enum_v<std::decay_t<E>>).
Compilation requires magic_enum to support char-based string_view; enforced by static_assert: magic_enum::string_view::value_type must be char.
Behavior depends on magic_enum support for the enum type; unsupported or unnamed values will be converted via magic_enum::enum_integer and formatted with std::to_string.
No run-time preconditions on e beyond being a valid object of enum type E.

functions.name: std::formatter::format
functions.signature:
template <typename E>
template <class FormatContext>
auto std::formatter<E, std::enable_if_t<std::is_enum_v<std::decay_t<E>>, char>>::format(E e, FormatContext& ctx) const
functions.description: Formats an enum value e into a std::format output context by delegating to std::formatter<std::string_view, char> with the string produced by magic_enum::detail::format_as(e). Use implicitly via std::format/format_to with enum arguments to print either the enumerator name (or flags composition) when available, otherwise the integer value.
requirements: Available only when __cpp_lib_format is defined (C++20 <format> support).
This specialization participates only when E is an enum type (std::is_enum_v<std::decay_t<E>>).
FormatContext must be a valid std::format context type; typically std::format_context or w/o wide char since char is used.
The resulting formatting behavior and names depend on magic_enum’s ability to reflect the enum; unsupported values are formatted as their integer.
The char type of the formatter is char (second template parameter resolves to char).

functions.name: fmt::formatter::format
functions.signature:
template <typename E>
template <class FormatContext>
auto fmt::formatter<E, std::enable_if_t<std::is_enum_v<std::decay_t<E>>, char>>::format(E e, FormatContext& ctx) const
functions.description: Formats an enum value e into a {fmt} output context by delegating to fmt::formatter<std::string_view, char> with the string produced by magic_enum::detail::format_as(e). Use implicitly via fmt::format/format_to with enum arguments to print enumerator names or flags composition when available, otherwise the integer value.
requirements: Available only when FMT_VERSION is defined (the {fmt} library is present).
This specialization participates only when E is an enum type (std::is_enum_v<std::decay_t<E>>).
FormatContext must be a valid {fmt} formatting context (e.g., fmt::format_context) using char.
Behavior depends on magic_enum’s ability to reflect the enum; unsupported values are formatted as their integer.
The char type of the formatter is char (second template parameter resolves to char).

functions.name: magic_enum::enum_fuse
functions.signature:
template <typename... Es>
[[nodiscard]] constexpr auto magic_enum::enum_fuse(Es... values) noexcept
functions.description: Computes a bijective fused key from two or more enum values, suitable for implementing multi-dimensional switch/case or lookup dispatch. Returns an optional fused token: by default a typesafe opaque enum class backed by std::uintmax_t (when typesafe mode is enabled), or optional<std::uintmax_t> when MAGIC_ENUM_NO_TYPESAFE_ENUM_FUSE is defined. The result is empty if any input value is not a valid enumerator recognized by magic_enum. Usable in constexpr contexts and marked [[nodiscard]] to encourage checking the result.
requirements: All template parameters Es (after std::decay_t) must be enum types (enforced by static_assert).
At least 2 arguments must be provided (enforced by static_assert).

The sum of detail::log2(enum_count<std::decay_t<Es>>() + 1) over all Es must be <= (sizeof(std::uintmax_t) * 8); otherwise the call is ill-formed due to static_assert (large enums not supported for fusion).
Each provided value must be a valid enumerator for its enum type (magic_enum::enum_index(value) must succeed); otherwise the function returns an empty optional and may trip MAGIC_ENUM_ASSERT(fuse).
Callers should handle the returned optional (function is [[nodiscard]]).
The function is noexcept; no exceptions are thrown.
Return type depends on configuration: optional<std::uintmax_t> if MAGIC_ENUM_NO_TYPESAFE_ENUM_FUSE is defined; otherwise an optional of an internal enum class wrapping std::uintmax_t.

functions.name: magic_enum::ostream_operators::operator<<
functions.signature:
template <typename Char, typename Traits, typename E, detail::enable_if_t<E, int> = 0>
std::basic_ostream<Char, Traits>& operator<<(std::basic_ostream<Char, Traits>& os, E value);
functions.description: Stream insertion for enum values. If the enum type E is supported by magic_enum, writes the enum's name to the stream; for flag enums, writes the combined flags name. If no name is available or the type is unsupported, falls back to writing the underlying integer value. Usage: include this header and use operator<< with a std::basic_ostream of matching Char/Traits and an enum value.
requirements: E is an enum type (enforced via SFINAE by detail::enable_if_t<E, int>).
If magic_enum recognizes E (detail::supported<E>::value), the textual name is emitted; otherwise the underlying integer value is written.
For flag enums (detail::subtype_v<E> == enum_subtype::flags), combined flag names are emitted when resolvable; otherwise falls back to integer output.
The stream os must be a valid std::basic_ostream<Char, Traits>; output occurs via os.put or formatted integer output.
No text is written if name lookup fails? (Not applicable: in this overload, fallback to integer is always written when name lookup fails).
Caller should expect standard stream error handling semantics (e.g., badbit/failbit can be set by the stream on I/O errors).

functions.name: magic_enum::istream_operators::operator>>
functions.signature:
template <typename Char, typename Traits, typename E, detail::enable_if_t<E, int> = 0>
std::basic_istream<Char, Traits>& operator>>(std::basic_istream<Char, Traits>& is, E& value);
functions.description: Stream extraction for enum values. Reads a token into a basic_string<Char, Traits> and attempts to parse it as an enum name. For supported enums, sets value to the parsed enum; for flag enums, parses combined flag names. On parse failure or unsupported enum types, sets the stream's failbit.
requirements: E is an enum type (enforced via SFINAE by detail::enable_if_t<E, int>).
Input is read as a single token using operator>>(std::basic_string<Char, Traits>&); whitespace-delimited.
For supported non-flag enums, the token must match a valid enum name as recognized by magic_enum::enum_cast<E>(string).
For supported flag enums, the token must match a valid flags representation as recognized by magic_enum::enum_flags_cast<E>(string).
If parsing fails or E is not supported by magic_enum, is.setstate(std::basic_ios<Char>::failbit) is called; callers should check stream state or have exceptions set appropriately.
The stream is must be a valid std::basic_istream<Char, Traits> and supply characters compatible with Char/Traits.

functions.name: magic_enum::enum_switch
functions.signature:
template <typename Result = magic_enum::detail::default_result_type, typename E, magic_enum::detail::enum_subtype S = magic_enum::detail::subtype_v<E>, typename F, typename R = magic_enum::detail::result_t<E, S, Result, F>>
constexpr decltype(auto) magic_enum::enum_switch(F&& f, E value);
functions.description: Compile-time-like switch over an enum value that invokes the callable f with an enum_constant corresponding to value. The return type R is deduced from invoking f over all reflected enumerators of E (or constrained to Result if provided). If value does not correspond to a reflected enumerator or the case is not invocable with the required return type, a default result is returned (default-constructed R, or no-op if R is void). Intended for efficient, type-safe dispatch over enum values without a traditional switch.
requirements: E must be an enum type (enforced by static_assert).
E must be a reflected enum for the chosen subtype S (detail::is_reflected_v<E, S> must be true).

F must be invocable with magic_enum::enum_constant<V> for every reflected enumerator V of E and produce a common result type; otherwise the function template is not viable (constrained via detail::result_t).
If Result is explicitly specified, it must be convertible to/from the deduced common invocation result; otherwise substitution fails.
If value does not match any reflected enumerator in subtype S, a default result is produced (default-constructed R, or void).
This overload is available regardless of hash-related macros; internally it selects an implementation depending on MAGIC_ENUM_ENABLE_HASH or MAGIC_ENUM_ENABLE_HASH_SWITCH.

functions.name: magic_enum::detail::constexpr_switch_impl
functions.signature:
template <std::size_t I, std::size_t End, typename R, typename E, magic_enum::detail::enum_subtype S, typename F, typename Def>
constexpr decltype(auto) magic_enum::detail::constexpr_switch_impl(F&& f, E value, Def&& def);
functions.description: Internal recursive implementation used to dispatch over the reflected enumerators of E. Compares value against the I-th reflected enumerator (within subtype S) and, on match, invokes f(enum_constant<V>) and returns it cast to R; otherwise recurses. If no match is found or the invocation is not valid for R, calls def() to produce a fallback result.
requirements: Only available when neither MAGIC_ENUM_ENABLE_HASH nor MAGIC_ENUM_ENABLE_HASH_SWITCH is defined (it is conditionally compiled out otherwise).
E must be an enum type for correct usage (the public wrapper enforces this; this function assumes it).
F should be callable as R f(enum_constant<V>) for matching cases; if not, def() is used instead.
Def must be a nullary callable that returns a value convertible to R; it is invoked when no enumerator matches or when the corresponding invocation is not valid for R.
Indices must satisfy 0 <= I <= End; typically driven by the library with End == count_v<E, S>.

functions.name: magic_enum::detail::constexpr_switch
functions.signature:
template <typename R, typename E, magic_enum::detail::enum_subtype S, typename F, typename Def>
constexpr decltype(auto) magic_enum::detail::constexpr_switch(F&& f, E value, Def&& def);
functions.description: Internal entry point that dispatches to constexpr_switch_impl over all reflected enumerators of E for subtype S. If there are no reflected values (count_v<E, S> == 0), it immediately calls def(). Otherwise, it attempts to match value and invoke f(enum_constant<V>) with result cast to R, falling back to def() when no match or invalid invocation for R occurs.
requirements: Only available when neither MAGIC_ENUM_ENABLE_HASH nor MAGIC_ENUM_ENABLE_HASH_SWITCH is defined (it is conditionally compiled out otherwise).
E must be an enum type (enforced by static_assert).
Def must be a nullary callable returning a value convertible to R; it is used when no enumerators are reflected or when no match/invocation is possible.
F should be callable as R f(enum_constant<V>) for matching cases; otherwise def() is used.

functions.name: magic_enum::enum_for_each
functions.signature:
template <typename E, detail::enum_subtype S = detail::subtype_v<E>, typename F, detail::enable_if_t<E, int> = 0>
constexpr auto enum_for_each(F&& f)
functions.description: Iterates over all reflected enumerator values of enum E (for subtype S) and invokes the callable f with a magic_enum::enum_constant<V> for each enumerator V. Intended for compile-time or run-time enumeration processing without manually listing values. Return type depends on f: if any invocation returns void, the function returns void; if all invocations return the same non-void type T, returns std::array<T, count>; otherwise returns std::tuple of the individual return types in declaration order.
requirements: E must be an enum type (enforced by static_assert).
E must be reflectable by magic_enum for the chosen subtype S (detail::is_reflected_v<E,S> must be true; requires valid enum_range).
F must be invocable for every enumerator: F must be callable with arguments of type magic_enum::enum_constant<values_v<E,S>[I]> for all I in [0, count).
The function participates in overload resolution only when detail::enable_if_t<E, int> is valid (typically when E is an enum supported by magic_enum).

If any invocation of F yields void, the overall return type is void; if all are non-void and the same type T, the return is std::array<T, count>; otherwise the return is std::tuple of the per-invocation return types.
Callers must include magic_enum and ensure that enum_range (or equivalent reflection configuration) for E is available so values_v/count_v are defined.

functions.name: magic_enum::enum_next_value
functions.signature:
template <typename E, detail::enum_subtype S = detail::subtype_v<E>>
[[nodiscard]] constexpr auto enum_next_value(E value, std::ptrdiff_t n = 1) noexcept -> detail::enable_if_t<E, optional<std::decay_t<E>>>
functions.description: Returns the n-th next enumerator of E (for subtype S) relative to value, if it exists in the reflected set; otherwise returns an empty optional. Useful for stepping forward through the reflected enumerators without wrapping around.
requirements: E must be an enum type and reflectable by magic_enum for subtype S (values_v/count_v available).
value should be one of the reflected enumerators of E; if not, the return is empty optional.
n may be positive, zero, or negative; the computed target index (current_index + n) must fall within [0, count) for a non-empty result.
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept); callers should handle the empty optional case.
If the enum has zero reflected values, the function always returns an empty optional.

functions.name: magic_enum::enum_next_value_circular
functions.signature:
template <typename E, detail::enum_subtype S = detail::subtype_v<E>>
[[nodiscard]] constexpr auto enum_next_value_circular(E value, std::ptrdiff_t n = 1) noexcept -> detail::enable_if_t<E, std::decay_t<E>>
functions.description: Returns the n-th next enumerator of E (for subtype S) relative to value, wrapping around circularly using modulo arithmetic. If value is not a reflected enumerator (or reflection is unavailable), the function triggers an assertion via MAGIC_ENUM_ASSERT and returns value.
requirements: E must be an enum type and reflectable by magic_enum for subtype S (values_v/count_v available) for defined, non-asserting behavior.
value must be one of the reflected enumerators for wraparound semantics to apply.
n may be positive, zero, or negative; stepping is performed modulo the reflected enumerator count.
Callers should not rely on the fallback of returning the input value when value is not reflected; this path asserts (debug) and indicates misuse.
Function is noexcept; callers cannot rely on exceptions for error signaling.

functions.name: magic_enum::enum_prev_value
functions.signature:
template <typename E, detail::enum_subtype S = detail::subtype_v<E>>
[[nodiscard]] constexpr auto enum_prev_value(E value, std::ptrdiff_t n = 1) noexcept -> detail::enable_if_t<E, optional<std::decay_t<E>>>
functions.description: Returns the n-th previous enumerator of E (for subtype S) relative to value, if it exists in the reflected set; otherwise returns an empty optional. Equivalent to enum_next_value with negative step but expressed for reverse traversal.
requirements: E must be an enum type and reflectable by magic_enum for subtype S.
value should be one of the reflected enumerators of E; otherwise returns empty optional.
n may be positive, zero, or negative; the computed target index (current_index - n) must fall within [0, count) for a non-empty result.
No exceptions are thrown (noexcept); callers must handle the empty optional when stepping would go out of bounds.
If the enum has zero reflected values, the function always returns an empty optional.

functions.name: magic_enum::enum_prev_value_circular
functions.signature:
template <typename E, detail::enum_subtype S = detail::subtype_v<E>>
[[nodiscard]] constexpr auto enum_prev_value_circular(E value, std::ptrdiff_t n = 1) noexcept -> detail::enable_if_t<E, std::decay_t<E>>
functions.description: Returns the n-th previous enumerator of E (for subtype S) relative to value, wrapping around circularly using modulo arithmetic. If value is not a reflected enumerator (or reflection is unavailable), the function triggers an assertion via MAGIC_ENUM_ASSERT and returns value.
requirements: E must be an enum type and reflectable by magic_enum for subtype S for defined behavior.
value must be one of the reflected enumerators for wraparound semantics to apply.
n may be positive, zero, or negative; stepping is performed modulo the reflected enumerator count.
On invalid input (unreflected value or empty reflection), behavior asserts in debug builds and returns the input value; callers should avoid relying on this path.
Function is noexcept; callers cannot use exceptions for error handling.

functions.name: magic_enum::customize::adl_info
functions.signature: constexpr magic_enum::customize::adl_info_holder<> magic_enum::customize::adl_info()

requirements: E must be an enum type supported by magic_enum on the current compiler.

data_types.description: A whitespace-delimited textual token representing an enum value name as parsed by magic_enum::enum_cast and related operators. Examples include exact enumerator identifiers like "Red" or "Green" for an enum Color, and for flags-capable enums possibly combined names separated by a delimiter (commonly '|'), e.g., "Read|Write". Parsing is case-sensitive unless a case-insensitive comparator is configured. Any non-matching token should cause parse failure (e.g., stream failbit in operator>>).

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: enum name token
# Target stub reads a single whitespace-delimited token from a narrow stringstream
# and attempts to parse it as one of two enums:
#   enum class Color { Red = 0, Green = 1, Blue = 2 };
#   enum Animal { Dog = 0, Cat = 1, Bird = 2 };
# magic_enum::istream_operators::operator>> expects exact enumerator names for non-flags enums.
# So valid tokens include: Red, Green, Blue, Dog, Cat, Bird.
# The stream reads a single token until whitespace; we should provide a string (no newlines inside token).
# We generate interesting tokens to exercise behaviors:
#  - exact matches for both enums
#  - case variations (should fail)
#  - unknown names (should fail)
#  - very long but single token (should be truncated by stub to 1024)
#  - tokens with separators like '|' (flags-like, should fail for these enums)
#  - tokens with leading/trailing spaces are not part of the token since FUZZ_PARAM_STR returns raw data; the stub
#    constructs istringstream(token) and operator>> reads the whole string as a single token if it contains no spaces.
# Therefore we avoid internal whitespace to ensure one token is read; to test failbit we use mismatched strings.

_VALID_COLOR = ["Red", "Green", "Blue"]
_VALID_ANIMAL = ["Dog", "Cat", "Bird"]
_ALL_VALID = _VALID_COLOR + _VALID_ANIMAL

def _random_case_variant(s: str, rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    return ''.join(ch.upper() if rnd.choice([True, False]) else ch.lower() for ch in s)

def _random_unknown(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a plausible identifier that's not in the valid set.
    # Ensure it doesn't accidentally match.
    while True:
        length = rnd.randint(3, 10)
        s = rnd.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
        s += ''.join(rnd.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(length - 1))
        if s not in _ALL_VALID:
            return s

def _long_token(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a long token (>1024) to exercise truncation in stub.
    base = rnd.choice(_ALL_VALID)
    pad_len = rnd.randint(1100, 1500)
    # Use only non-space printable ascii to avoid token splitting.
    pad_chars = ''.join(rnd.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-.:/") for _ in range(pad_len))
    return base + pad_chars

def _flags_like(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Combine valid names with '|', which should fail for these non-flags enums.
    parts = rnd.sample(_ALL_VALID, rnd.randint(2, 3))
    return '|'.join(parts)

def _mixed_known_unknown(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    return rnd.choice(_ALL_VALID) + rnd.choice(["_X", "123", "Extra"])  # still single token

def _ambiguous_prefix(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce prefixes or suffixes that might look like names but aren't exact matches.
    base = rnd.choice(_ALL_VALID)
    if rnd.choice([True, False]):
        # prefix extra char
        return rnd.choice(string.ascii_letters) + base
    else:
        return base + rnd.choice(string.ascii_letters)

_generators = [
    # Exact matches
    lambda r: r.choice(_ALL_VALID),
    # Case-variant mismatches
    lambda r: _random_case_variant(r.choice(_ALL_VALID), r),
    # Unknown identifier
    _random_unknown,
    # Long token to trigger truncation
    _long_token,
    # Flags-like composition
    _flags_like,
    # Mixed known with trailing stuff
    _mixed_known_unknown,
    # Ambiguous prefix/suffix
    _ambiguous_prefix,
]

# Ensure total length <= 4096 bytes as required.
_MAX_BYTES = 4096

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose one of the scenario generators with weighted probabilities to favor valid names too.
    weights = [
        3,  # exact valid
        2,  # case variant (likely invalid)
        2,  # unknown
        1,  # long token
        1,  # flags-like
        1,  # mixed
        1,  # ambiguous
    ]
    idx = rnd.choices(range(len(_generators)), weights=weights, k=1)[0]
    token = _generators[idx](rnd)

    # Clamp to 4096 bytes overall.
    b = token.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) > _MAX_BYTES:
        b = b[:_MAX_BYTES]
    return b
